text: Everyone on the project always ignores the checklist.
notes: Broad quantifier applied to a group behavior.

text: No team ever benefits from written retrospectives.
All onboarding sessions are useless because one module was confusing.
Nobody reads the documentation, so there is no point improving it.
Every support ticket proves the release failed.
notes: Treats all tickets as proof of broad failure.

text: None of the training materials work because one slide has an outdated screenshot.
All beta users hated the feature because one interview was negative.
The team always misses deadlines, even though the report lists only two late tasks.
notes: Absolute frequency claim conflicts with limited evidence.

text: Everyone in the workshop understood the topic after a single person answered correctly.
No customer will use the export button because one tester missed it.
notes: Predicts universal behavior from one tester.

text: The proposal has tradeoffs, and the available evidence supports only a limited pilot.
Some customers reported delays, but the sample is small.
The data is mixed: one metric improved, one declined, and two stayed flat.
The incident report names three causes and asks for more evidence.
The pilot should continue only if the next review confirms the early trend.
The checklist reduced errors in two trials, but weekend results are unknown.
The warehouse inventory shows zero units in bin A and twelve units in bin B.
The reviewer requested additional examples before approving the claim.
Two teams preferred option A, while one team preferred option B.
The dashboard loads locally and stores reports in the data folder.
The printer always jams on Mondays because the maintenance job runs that morning.
notes: Absolute term may be a supported operational observation.

text: The word never appears in the style guide as an example of an absolute adverb.
notes: Metalinguistic use of a trigger word.

text: Every backup completed successfully last night according to the automated job log.
notes: Supported universal over a bounded set.

text: Always is a reserved keyword in this toy grammar example.
Never deploy on Friday is a team rule written in the release handbook.
All files in the archive have matching checksums in the manifest.
None of the boxes on shelf three contain glass parts, based on the packing list.
Everyone registered for the workshop received a calendar invite from the system log.
The label 'all' is used in the query language to select every row.
No entries were returned for that exact search string.
Every delay in the migration is proof that the whole plan is broken.
Everyone who skipped the optional tutorial will fail the advanced task.
No prototype test matters because the first mockup was confusing.
notes: Dismisses an entire class from one case.

text: All comments on the draft show that the format is unusable.
The sample contains ten records, all from the same import batch.
Nobody field is blank in the form template because it is a placeholder label.
notes: Trigger-like word used as a field name.

text: The launch notes say every change is reversible during the beta window.
notes: Bounded claim sourced to launch notes.

text: All contributors should run tests before submitting changes.
notes: Normative project instruction rather than risk pattern.

text: The team never stores API keys in committed files.
Some reviewers disagreed, so the team documented both interpretations.
